$comment: PE/COFF relocatable object (.obj) for x86_64 Windows. Second shipped object-format JSON (plan 14 LK2 cycle 1, 2026-05-29). Consumed by `src/link/format/pe.cpp` via the format-blind linker engine. Section Characteristics + IMAGE_FILE_HEADER fields + IMAGE_RELOCATION type values follow the Microsoft PE/COFF spec (PE Format on Microsoft Learn).
$stackReserveUnsupportedReasonComment: D-SQLITE-PE64-FULL-TIER-STACK-DEPTH: this artifact form has NO image header field for a stack size (a relocatable object / static archive is an INPUT to a later link, not a loadable program), so a `stackReserve` / `--stack-reserve` request against it is REFUSED with an actionable remedy -- request the reserve on the build that produces the final EXECUTABLE image -- rather than silently dropped.
$dataModelComment: FC3 c1: 64-bit Windows is LLP64 (int 32, long 32, long long 64, ptr 64). Consumed by the semantic tier (buildCuMir threads format.dataModel() into analyze()): c long binds I32 here, the literal ladder + descriptor signatureByDataModel resolve their LLP64 arms. REQUIRED closed-enum field; the loader rejects a missing or unknown value (a silent default would bake wrong widths).
$headerNameMatchingComment: D-PP-HEADER-CASE-INSENSITIVE-PE: Windows filesystems (NTFS, FAT) match file names case-INSENSITIVELY, and the Windows SDK depends on it -- sqlite3.c:67322 spells `#include <Windows.h>` with a capital W while the shipped descriptor is `windows.json`. REQUIRED closed-enum field. DSS ASCII-folds the comparison ITSELF per path component (core/types/include_path_resolve.cpp) instead of asking fs::exists, so this resolves identically whether the build host is NTFS or ext4 -- MEASURED before the axis existed: rc=0 through /mnt/c, rc=1 error[F001A] on ext4, SAME binary, SAME commit.
$cSymbolDecorationComment: D-FFI-CMANGLING-RULE-NOT-CONFIG-DRIVEN: PE/COFF x64 applies NO decoration to a C identifier. The leading-underscore cdecl convention belongs to 32-bit x86 PE, which DSS does not ship; the 32-bit `_func` and stdcall `_func@N` rules arrive as their own scheme enumerators WITH their engine arms, never as a re-spelling of this one. MEASURED 2026-08-06 (`objdump -p C:/Windows/System32/ucrtbase.dll`, GNU binutils via WSL): the UCRT exports `exit`, `_exit` AND `_Exit` as three DISTINCT entries -- so the underscored spelling is not a decoration of `exit` here either, it already names a different function, and a format that wrongly claimed `leading-underscore` would silently bind to it. Consistent with this family's own `processExit.importMangledName`, the undecorated `exit`. This key is the single owner of a fact that previously had TWO: the closed C++ table `kCManglingRules` (src/ffi/mangling/c_mangle.cpp, keyed on ObjectFormatKind) and, redundantly, a literal encoding in the descriptors themselves -- the macho64-*-exec files spell `processExit.importMangledName` as `_exit` while their elf/pe siblings spell it `exit`. Two owners in two languages, with nothing forcing them to agree. RED-ON-DISABLE, stated precisely for the tier that exists today (MEASURED 2026-08-06 by actually removing the key from a shipped file and running the suite): DELETE this key and the format is REFUSED AT LOAD -- TWO errors at /cSymbolDecoration, one C_MissingField from the loader and one from ObjectFormatData::validate(), which loadFromText runs before returning -- so every test and example that loads this format goes red, naming the file. CHANGING the value is now an equally REAL lever, and this sentence was corrected the moment it became true: before step C4 the engine still read a C++ table and the value here changed no emitted binary. C4 landed (same cycle, TF-C122), and the effect is MEASURED 2026-08-06 -- flipping macho64-arm64-darwin-exec from `leading-underscore` to `none` and RECOMPILING NOTHING made the engine emit `printf` where it had emitted `_printf`, reddening tests/ffi/test_c_mangle.cpp's SchemeIsReadFromTheShippedSchemaNotACppTable. That is the whole point of the anchor: the answer lives in this file, so editing this file changes what the compiler emits. Two further pins guard the value: tests/link/test_c_symbol_decoration.cpp asserts the per-kind answer across all 24 shipped files and cross-checks it against this family's own processExit.importMangledName.
$cCallingConventionComment: D-FFI-ABI-CATALOG-SELECTS-CALLING-CONVENTION-BY-FORMAT-IDENTITY: the platform C ABI for code compiled into this format, NAMING a row in the paired target's callingConventions[] array. Microsoft x64 (`rcx,rdx,r8,r9` + 32 bytes of shadow space) — the SAME x86_64 processor as the elf64/macho64 descriptors, a DIFFERENT convention, which is why the fact is per-FORMAT and cannot live on the target.
$outputExtensionComment: D-PROGRAM-TIER-RETAINS-FORMAT-IDENTITY-BRANCHES: the extension the driver appends to an artifact this format produces. This used to be derived in C++ by `program/target_spec.cpp::outputExtensionFor`, a five-arm `switch (fmt.kind())` with a NESTED per-flavor switch inside each arm -- seven identity mentions computing a NAMING fact, which is not an engine behaviour at all. The nest existed because one ObjectFormatKind spans several artifact flavors; a DOCUMENT is exactly one flavor, so the whole derivation collapses to this one string. REQUIRED on every format. An EMPTY value is a DECLARED answer and not an omission -- a Unix executable carries no extension -- which is why the in-memory field is an `optional` and the loader's required check asks `contains`, never `empty`.
$archiveFlavorComment: D-PROGRAM-TIER-RETAINS-FORMAT-IDENTITY-BRANCHES: WHICH `ar` variant this format's ECOSYSTEM uses. Declared on every native format, not only the `container: archive` ones, because that is what the deleted C++ derivation answered: `(format.kind() == ObjectFormatKind::Pe) ? Coff : SysV` was handed WHATEVER format the caller had, and `linkAndWriteStaticArchive` is reachable with the RELOCATABLE format of an ecosystem as well as its archive one (MEASURED -- restricting the key to archives reddened link/test_ar_writer and program/test_static_link). NOT cosmetic: the coff flavor carries the little-endian second linker member link.exe requires to resolve members at all. A closed VERB rather than an open name, because an archive layout is an ENGINE capability -- only variants `writeArArchive` realizes can be honored.
$targetArchComment: D-PROGRAM-TIER-RETAINS-FORMAT-IDENTITY-BRANCHES: the .target.json NAME this format is for. `crossValidateTargetFormat` compares it against TargetSchema::name() -- two DECLARED NAMES -- where it used to run a six-arm `switch (format.kind())` reading a DIFFERENT field per identity (elf.machine / pe.machine / macho.cputype) and compare each against a hardcoded C++ table, kTargetArchMachineCodes, keyed on (target name x format kind). THAT TABLE IS DELETED, and the argument is ONE OWNER rather than tidiness: `arm64 is EM_AARCH64 = 183` had two owners -- this document's own machine field and that C++ row -- with nothing forcing them to agree, which is the identical shape as kCManglingRules and kAbiCatalog. The number now lives only in the document that emits it, and the pairing question is answered by a name this document states outright. Adding a new arch is now JSON-ONLY.
$predefinedMacrosComment: TF-C97 (D-PP-FORMAT-DATA-MODEL-PREDEFINES): THIS FORMAT DELIBERATELY DECLARES NO `predefinedMacros`, and the absence is an ANSWER rather than an omission -- it is the whole reason the channel lives on the FORMAT and not on the target. `dataModel` above is LLP64, so `__LP64__`/`_LP64` must NOT be defined here: MEASURED 2026-07-30, `/usr/bin/clang -dM -E -x c /dev/null -target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` (Apple clang 21.0.0) defines NEITHER, while the SAME clang defines BOTH on x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu and x86_64-apple-darwin -- the same CPU, differing only by object format, which is precisely why a target-side row would be a lie on this leg. Adding either spelling here would make the Windows headers take their LP64 arms against a 32-bit `long`. Pinned in the NEGATIVE direction by tests/link/test_object_format_schema.cpp.
$bitFieldStrategyComment: D-CSUBSET-BITFIELD-ABI-EXACT: MSVC x64 bit-field packing (byte-ABI-exact to cl.exe). The strategy is OS/format-determined (x86_64 serves both PE and ELF), so it lives on the format, not the target. See pe64-x86_64-windows-exec for the full rule.
$unnamedBitFieldAlignmentComment: D-CSUBSET-ZERO-WIDTH-BITFIELD-ALIGNMENT: an UNNAMED bit-field contributes NO alignment. MEASURED with cl.exe 19.51 (`_Static_assert` on sizeof AND __alignof): `struct { char c; unsigned :0; char d; }` is 2/1. ~ DECLARED FOR COMPLETENESS AND DELIBERATELY NOT LOAD-BEARING: `msvc_straddle` never reads this key, because the MSVC rule is a property OF that strategy -- a zero-width field is INERT unless it terminates an open allocation unit, and when it does it folds its type's alignment and bumps the high-water. That is measured identical on x64 and arm64 PE, so there is nothing per-format left to declare. The key is stated so this document answers the same question every other C-ABI format answers, rather than being silently exempt for a reason a reader would have to reconstruct.
$longDoubleFormatComment: FC17.9(e) D-CSUBSET-LONG-DOUBLE: MSVC x64 `long double` IS `double` (64-bit IEEE, 8/8) — the f64 axis collapses the c `long double` row to F64. See pe64-x86_64-windows-exec for the full rationale.
$externCallDispatchComment: D-LK-PE-OBJECT-WEAK-FUNCTION-ADDR-REL32-TO-AN-ABSOLUTE-TARGET (P54) REPLACED `direct-plt` HERE, AND THE SENTENCE IT REPLACED IS KEPT BECAUSE IT WAS TRUE OF EVERY STRONG IMPORT AND FALSE OF EXACTLY ONE CASE. It read (D-LK-OBJECT-EXTERN-CALL-RELOCATABLE, c148): extern FUNCTION calls lower into this relocatable .obj as a plain direct `call rel32` (E8 disp32) + an IMAGE_REL_AMD64_REL32 against an UNDEFINED COFF symbol carrying its REAL import name — PE x64 C mangling is IDENTITY, so `puts` is emitted verbatim — and `the FINAL linker resolves it either directly to a same-link definition or through an import thunk it synthesizes for a DLL import`. ⚠ THAT LAST CLAUSE IS FALSE FOR A WEAK REFERENCE, ✔MEASURED 2026-09-02: a COFF weak external's fallback is an ABSOLUTE symbol of value 0, no 32-bit PC-relative displacement reaches an absolute from a 0x140000000 image base, and link.exe 14.51 answers `LNK2016: absolute symbol maybe used as target of REL32 relocation` — TWICE on the DSS object (once for the address lea, once for the call) and ONCE on mingw-w64 gcc 13.2.0's OWN object, which routes the address through `.refptr.maybe` but keeps the call direct. mingw `ld` links both rc 0 with no diagnostic after TRUNCATING the displacement to 0x100000000. clang 18.1.3 routes BOTH references through `.refptr.maybe` on --target=x86_64-pc-windows-msvc AND on --target=x86_64-w64-windows-gnu, and link.exe links THAT rc 0 — so the indirect shape is the one all three consumers accept, and an object DSS emits must link where clang's does. `indirect-slot` makes the call site `call qword ptr [rip+sym]` (FF 15 disp32), whose relocation the linker retargets from the import to the `.refptr.<name>` slot it mints per `objectImportSlot` below; that same slot is where MIR→LIR's GlobalAddr arm now LOADS the function's address from, so the address form and the call form name ONE place and the link tier never has to tell a `&f` relocation from an `f()` one — which it cannot, both being a pc-relative reloc against the same symbol. ★ THE COST IS ONE LOAD PER EXTERN CALL, AND IT IS DECLARED UNCONDITIONALLY RATHER THAN NARROWED TO WEAK IMPORTS: this key states how an extern's identity is REACHED in artifacts of this format, and a per-symbol exception would make two shapes answer one question — the same reason `dataImportBinding` below is unconditional. ⓘ The EXEC/DLL siblings keep `direct-plt` and must: their walker synthesizes a `jmp *[IAT slot]` thunk and points each extern's VA at it, so there `&f` is already a callable code address and a deref would read the stub's bytes. D-FFI-EXTERN-CALL-DISPATCH + D-FFI-PE-IMPORT-THUNK + D-LK-OBJECT-EXTERN-CALL-RELOCATABLE.
$indirectSlotBindingsComment: D-LK-PE-OBJECT-STRONG-EXTERN-PAYS-THE-WEAK-IMPORTS-SLOT (P55): WHICH imports the `indirect-slot` shape above applies to. ⚠⚠ THE SENTENCE IT NARROWS IS PRESERVED VERBATIM IN THE KEY ABOVE AND WAS RIGHT ABOUT THE DEFECT AND WRONG ABOUT THE SCOPE — it reads `THE COST IS ONE LOAD PER EXTERN CALL, AND IT IS DECLARED UNCONDITIONALLY RATHER THAN NARROWED TO WEAK IMPORTS: this key states how an extern's identity is REACHED in artifacts of this format, and a per-symbol exception would make two shapes answer one question`. ✔MEASURED 2026-09-02 that the unconditional form charged a STRONG import the full price for nothing: the strong twin of that key's own fixture — `weak` the ONLY variable — emitted the IDENTICAL object, one `FF 15` call site and one 8-byte `.refptr.maybe` COMDAT, and a 10-import translation unit carried 15 `FF 15` sites and 11 `.refptr` COMDATs of which ZERO were needed. ★ THE NARROWING AXIS IS NOT A DSS CHOICE — ALL THREE REFERENCES USE IT FOR FUNCTIONS, each probed separately with `weak` as the only variable: clang 18.1.3 `--target=x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` AND `--target=x86_64-w64-windows-gnu` both emit `.rdata$.refptr.maybe` + two `REL32 .refptr.maybe` for a WEAK extern function and, for the STRONG one, a plain direct `REL32 maybe` with NO `.refptr` section in the object at all; mingw-w64 gcc 13.2.0 the same (`.refptr.maybe` for the weak address, nothing for the strong); cl.exe has no source spelling for a weak import so it only ever emits the strong shape. ★★ AND THE REASON IS STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN STYLISTIC: a pc-relative relocation can only name a target that will have a SECTION and an address, and a COFF WEAK external's fallback is an ABSOLUTE value-0 symbol — the one resolution no rel32 reaches from a 0x140000000 image base. A GLOBAL undefined symbol has no such resolution: the final link either finds a definition or fails loud. So `weak` is exactly the set of bindings whose references cannot be direct here, which is why the key is keyed on SymbolBinding — the same agnostic vocabulary `ExternImport.binding` and `ModuleSymbol.binding` already speak — and not on anything PE-shaped. ⓘ `two shapes answer one question` WAS A REAL HAZARD AND IS NOT ONE ANY MORE, which is the whole content of the P55 change: the CALL-SITE shape used to be read off this format-level dispatch while the ADDRESS shape was read off a per-symbol set, so narrowing one without the other would have left a strong import's `FF 15` dereferencing its own address. Both halves now read ONE per-symbol answer (`ObjectFormatSchema::externRefTakesImportSlot`, which MIR→LIR and the linker's slot pass both consult), so there is exactly one shape per symbol and no way for the two tiers to disagree. ⚠ THIS DOES NOT NARROW `dataImportBinding` BELOW, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE: its unconditional slot has an INDEPENDENT measured reason recorded in its own key — `ld` refuses a direct rel32 against a symbol it must AUTO-IMPORT from a DLL — which is about DLL data, not about weakness, so this axis does not govern it. (The `same reason` clause in the key above, which tied the two, is the one clause of it that was inaccurate when written.) ⓘ An EMPTY list is refused at load rather than read as `nothing takes the slot` — that is a cancellation of the dispatch, not a narrowing of it — and so is `local`, which no import can ever carry.
$dataImportBindingComment: D-LK-PE-OBJECT-WEAK-DATA-EXTERN-REL32-TO-AN-ABSOLUTE-TARGET (P54): an extern DATA import's ADDRESS is LOADED from a pointer slot in an artifact of this format, never computed by a PC-relative displacement. ★★ THE REASON IS A MEASURED FOREIGN-LINK FAILURE, NOT SYMMETRY WITH THE EXEC SIBLING. A rel32 cannot reach an ABSOLUTE target, and a COFF weak external's fallback IS an absolute symbol of value 0 -- that is how COFF spells 'this reference resolved to nothing'. ✔MEASURED 2026-09-02 on a DSS `.obj` for `extern int ea __attribute__((weak)); if (&ea)`, whose `.text` carried `IMAGE_REL_AMD64_REL32 ea`: link.exe 14.51 REFUSES it (`LNK2016: absolute symbol 'ea' used as target of REL32 relocation`, twice, then LNK1165 -- no image); mingw GNU ld 13.2.0 links it rc 0 WITH NO DIAGNOSTIC having TRUNCATED the displacement, so the image computes 0x100000000 for an address that must be 0 and `if (&ea)` takes the wrong arm; lld-link does the same silently. The ELF twin is green and the DSS-linked PE exec returns 42, so the defect is INVISIBLE from inside the pipeline and appears only when a FOREIGN linker consumes the object. ★ WHAT THE REFERENCES DO, each probed separately, with `weak` as the ONLY variable on one triple: clang 18.1.3 `--target=x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` emits a direct `REL32 ea` for a STRONG extern and `REL32 .refptr.ea` + a `.rdata$.refptr.ea` COMDAT holding `ADDR64 ea` for a WEAK one; clang `--target=x86_64-w64-windows-gnu` and mingw-w64 gcc 13.2.0 emit `.refptr.<name>` for EVERY PE data extern; cl.exe 19.51 emits a direct REL32 and has no source spelling for a weak import, so it never meets the shape. ⚠ THE UNCONDITIONAL FORM IS DECLARED HERE RATHER THAN A WEAK-ONLY ONE, AND NOT BECAUSE IT WAS EASIER: `ld` refuses a direct rel32 against a symbol it must AUTO-IMPORT from a DLL, so the slot is what makes one emitted object linkable by link.exe, lld-link AND mingw ld -- which is the whole point of a relocatable artifact. The cost is one load per extern-data address materialization, which is the price both mingw references pay on every PE object. ⓘ The exec/dll siblings declare this SAME value for the SAME mechanism spelled differently: there the slot is the loader-filled `.idata` IAT entry the image walker mints. Here there is no import walker, so `objectImportSlot` below says how the object publishes the slot it carries ITSELF; the linker refuses a relocatable format that declares one key without the other.
$objectImportSlotComment: D-LK-PE-OBJECT-WEAK-DATA-EXTERN-REL32-TO-AN-ABSOLUTE-TARGET (P54): the SPELLING of the data-import slot this format's artifacts carry themselves. `.refptr.` is not a DSS invention -- it is what clang 18.1.3 emits on BOTH windows triples and what mingw-w64 gcc 13.2.0 emits for every PE data extern (✔MEASURED 2026-09-02), and matching it is load-bearing rather than cosmetic: the slot is a COMDAT, so a DSS object and a clang object that import one name publish the SAME key and the final linker folds them into ONE slot. A private prefix would silently produce two. ★ THE SLOT LANDS IN THE `relro` SECTION, whose row above names `.rdata` -- read-only data the link must still fix up, which is exactly what a pointer slot holding one IMAGE_REL_AMD64_ADDR64 is, and the same `.rdata` the references place `.refptr` in. ⚠ DSS does NOT spell the section `.rdata$.refptr.<name>` as they do: the `$` grouping is a link.exe SORT convention, the COMDAT key is the SYMBOL, and a name over 8 bytes would have to spill to the string table as `/nnnn` -- which DSS's own COFF reader refuses to classify, so DSS would emit objects it cannot read back. The ‘.’-led prefix cannot collide with a source symbol: no C identifier begins with one.
$weakDefinitionComment: D-CONFIG-WEAK-DEFINITION-DIALECT-NOT-DECLARED: HOW this format spells a WEAK DEFINITION -- a symbol several translation units may define, of which the linker keeps one. COFF has NO per-symbol weak storage class for a DEFINITION: IMAGE_SYM_CLASS_WEAK_EXTERNAL + its Auxiliary Format 3 record is a weak *REFERENCE* with a fallback alias (EXTERNAL storage class, UNDEF section number, value zero -- the /ALTERNATENAME shape), and it serves the separate ALIAS path. A weak DEFINITION here is a section flagged IMAGE_SCN_LNK_COMDAT whose Selection byte is IMAGE_COMDAT_SELECT_ANY -- "any section that defines the same COMDAT symbol can be linked; the rest are removed" -- which is exactly the semantics SymbolBinding::Weak carries. Verified against the published PE/COFF format, sections "Auxiliary Format 3: Weak Externals" and "COMDAT Sections (Object Only)"; the measured reference encodings that fix this choice (and the round trip through DSS's own COFF reader) live in the writer's weak-definition block in src/link/format/pe.cpp. THIS IS A DIALECT ROW, NOT A CAPABILITY FLAG: it says how this format spells something it CAN express, never that it cannot -- see D-LK-PE-ALTERNATENAME-DECLARE-AND-REFUSE for why an implementation gap recorded as a format incapability is a false fact in the place most likely to be trusted later. The .obj writer READS this key and refuses loud on a dialect it has no encoder for, so the declaration cannot drift away from what is actually emitted.
$runtimeLibrariesComment: D-CSUBSET-PACKED-ATOMIC-MEMBER (P54): the ROLE -> IMAGE table. ⚠ THIS TABLE'S EXISTENCE IS ITSELF A CORRECTION, AND THE SENTENCE IT CORRECTS IS PRESERVED IN $sehPersonalityOmittedComment BELOW RATHER THAN DELETED. That key argued the table was absent as a CONSEQUENCE and not as a second decision — 'with no sehPersonality, no processExit, no processArgs and no librarySynthesis on this format, NO block would name a role, and the loader refuses a table row that no block names as inert config. An empty table is the only self-consistent state.' Every clause was TRUE WHEN WRITTEN and the last one has since EXPIRED: P53 added a FIFTH role-naming block, `atomicsRuntime`, so a role can now be named on a format that declares none of those four spine blocks. The reasoning did not become wrong — its premise ran out ([[feedback-a-rows-premise-has-a-shelf-life]]), which nothing in either anchor gate can see. ★ THE UNWIND ABSENCE IS UNTOUCHED BY THIS ROW AND MUST STAY THAT WAY: `sehPersonality` and an `unwindPersonality` row remain deliberately absent for the MEASURED reason recorded below (the Obj arm emits no .pdata/.xdata, so declaring them trades a loud correct refusal for a silent drop — worse here than for the archive, since the object exists to be linked LATER and the final linker cannot notice unwind data was never emitted). Atomics and unwind are ORTHOGONAL questions about this format, and `tests/link/test_runtime_library_roles.cpp` now carries a SEPARATE per-flavour verdict for each rather than one boolean standing for both. ★★ P54 (D-C-ATOMICS-RUNTIME-IS-OURS-ON-PE64): A ROW'S SECOND CELL IS NOW A CHOICE OF TWO, NOT ONE STRING. `image` means the role is played by a PLATFORM IMAGE and its entries are IMPORTED; `source` means the role is played by a body DSS SHIPS AND COMPILES, and its entries are DEFINED IN THE PROGRAM. Exactly one per row, refused at load in both directions — neither is an unfilled role, both are two owners for one body. It is the SAME pair `shippedLibs/*.json` has carried for a year (`library` beside `realization`), lifted to the tier where ROLES live so that it also reaches a symbol the COMPILER MINTS, which has no descriptor row to hang off. A realized role resolves its spine block's derived path to the EMPTY STRING — the same `noLibraryBinding` shape `dirent`/`unistd` already use — so no lowerer, linker or writer learns the difference.
$atomicsRuntimeComment: D-CSUBSET-PACKED-ATOMIC-MEMBER (P54): the GENERIC C11 atomics entry points an UNDER-ALIGNED `_Atomic` scalar access lowers to a CALL of. The measurement that chose `libatomic-1.dll` over an in-box Microsoft image (there is none — ucrtbase, vcruntime140, kernel32, msvcrt and ntdll export ZERO `__atomic_*` between them), and the reason the reference union REQUIRES the libcall rather than gcc's inline pair, are argued in pe64-x86_64-windows-exec.format.json's copy of this key and are not restated here. ★ WHY A RELOCATABLE OBJECT DECLARES IT, when it resolves nothing itself: the object carries an UNDEFINED external for the entry names and the final link resolves them; the `libraryPath` this row supplies rides along on the `ExternImport` so the eventual image knows which DLL to name. That is exactly the shipped elf64-x86_64-linux (relocatable) arrangement, which declares `libatomic.so.1` on the same reasoning and likewise names no other role. ⚠ AND THE CONTRAST WITH THE UNWIND CASE IS THE WHOLE REASON THIS IS SAFE WHILE THAT ONE IS NOT: declaring `sehPersonality` here would let a `__try` compile to an object whose scope table was SILENTLY DROPPED, because the Obj arm has no emitter for it. There is no analogous silent drop for a call — `externCallDispatch: direct-plt` is already declared above and an extern call is exactly what this arm emits every day. The failure mode if the entry never resolves is an UNRESOLVED SYMBOL at the final link, which is loud, at the tier that can see it, and strictly better than the silent loss of atomicity the native pair would have shipped. ★★★ P54 LANE `la` — THE ROLE NO LONGER NAMES AN IMAGE, AND EVERY MEASUREMENT ABOVE STILL STANDS. Nothing above is refuted; what changed is the OPERATOR'S RULING on what to do about it. `libatomic-1.dll` really does export the generic entries, ucrtbase really exports none, and the union really does require the libcall route — but depending on a NON-IN-BOX, third-party image was ruled a workaround, and the row above now reads `source` instead of `image`: DSS SHIPS THE BODY, at `runtime/platform/src/atomic.c`, compiled by DSS for this very target and pulled out of the shipped runtime archive by the linker's ordinary unresolved-symbol walk. ⓘ THE PAY-PER-USE PROPERTY IS UNCHANGED AND STILL MEASURED: the archive member is pulled BY NAME, so a program that never lowers an under-aligned `_Atomic` never mentions `__atomic_load` and never links a byte of it. ⚠ AND THE DEPENDENCY-FLOOR PARAGRAPH ABOVE IS NOW HISTORY RATHER THAN A LIVE COST — it is preserved verbatim because it is the argument the ruling overturned, not because it still describes this format: a DSS pe64 program touching a packed `_Atomic` now imports `ucrtbase.dll` and nothing else. ⚠⚠ THE elf64 AND macho64 SIBLINGS DELIBERATELY KEEP THEIR `image` ROWS, and the reason is CORRECTNESS rather than inertia: `libatomic.so.1` and `libSystem.B.dylib` are those platforms' OWN atomics runtimes, so a gcc-built and a DSS-built translation unit touching the same under-aligned object reach the SAME arbiter. On aarch64 that arbiter is an address-hashed LOCK TABLE (the ISA has no bus lock — every aarch64 atomic primitive faults on an unaligned address), and a lock table arbitrates only between its own users, so shipping a private one there would be strictly WORSE than using the platform's. x86-64 has no such problem: DSS's body uses `lock`-prefixed read-modify-writes, which the ISA makes atomic against EVERY accessor regardless of alignment, so our body and mingw's libatomic interoperate.
$sehPersonalityOmittedComment: UCRT-P4 + D-LK-PE-OBJ-ARM-CARRIES-NO-UNWIND-INFO: THIS FORMAT DECLARES NEITHER `sehPersonality` NOR `runtimeLibraries`, AND THE ABSENCE IS A DECISION RATHER THAN AN UNFINISHED COPY OF THE exec/dll SIBLINGS. * WHAT CHANGED ON 2026-08-27, AND IT REVERSES THE OLD REASONING: this format's writer arm NOW EMITS `.pdata` + `.xdata`. Objects it produces are unwindable. ✔MEASURED on one non-leaf source with no `__try`: `.text` + `.xdata` 24 B + `.pdata` 36 B carrying 9 IMAGE_REL_AMD64_ADDR32NB relocations (three per RUNTIME_FUNCTION - two naming the function, one naming its `.xdata` blob, addends stamped in the section bytes because COFF has no addend column), and the object handed to MinGW ld produced an image whose EXCEPTION data directory grew by exactly those three 12-byte entries, each decoding to the prologue DSS actually emitted. Before that commit the same compile produced `.text` and nothing else, rc=0, not one diagnostic. * ⚠ TWO SENTENCES THAT USED TO STAND HERE WERE FALSE AND ARE DELETED, NOT SOFTENED. (1) 'AssembledFunction::unwind is nullopt on the object path by construction' - it never was: the ELF ET_REL arm reads that same field on that same path and writes `.eh_frame` 108 B + `.rela.eh_frame` 72 B from it. That sentence sent readers upstream to hunt a producer that was never missing, when the gap was in this format's WRITER. (2) 'SehScopeEntry is consumed ONLY by the image-side `.xdata` scope-table emitter in encodeExec' - true of the scope TABLE, but it was doing duty as an argument that no unwind information of any kind could reach an object, which is a different claim and a wrong one. * WHY THE TWO KEYS ARE STILL ABSENT, WHICH IS NOW A NARROWER AND HONEST REASON: a `__try` needs more than a frame description. Its SCOPE_TABLE states four RVAs per scope plus the personality handler's own, and `buildFunctionUnwindInfo` writes those as RESOLVED image addresses because the image walker was its only caller; in a relocatable object each is a relocation, not a value. So `pe::encode`'s Obj arm REFUSES a module whose functions carry `sehScopes`, loudly, and declaring `sehPersonality` here would buy nothing but that refusal arriving one phase later. Expressing the scope table as relocation requests is D-WIN64-SEH-FUNCLETS' subject; when it lands, these keys can be argued on their merits rather than blocked by a missing emitter. * ⚠ THE TRAP THE OLD TEXT WARNED ABOUT IS GONE: the `synthesizeSehFunclets` diagnostic used to end with 'Add the block', and following that advice here USED TO produce a silent miscompile (the compile succeeded, the tables vanished). It cannot any more - the writer emits the tables, and refuses the one shape it cannot yet relocate. * `runtimeLibraries` is absent as a CONSEQUENCE, not as a second decision: with no `sehPersonality`, no `processExit`, no `processArgs` and no `librarySynthesis` on this format, NO block would name a role, and the loader refuses a table row that no block names as inert config. An empty table is the only self-consistent state. * ENFORCED, not merely written: tests/link/test_runtime_library_roles.cpp `NoPeFormatNamesTheLegacyCrtInItsRoleTable` carries this format on an EXPLICIT exclusion list and asserts BOTH that the two keys stay absent AND that this rationale key stays non-empty - so the day they land here, that test goes red and forces the exclusion to be re-argued rather than silently widened. * THE FLAVOUR: a loose relocatable `.obj`, the direct analogue of `cl /c` and `gcc -c` output.
$supportedDataSectionsComment: D-LK-OBJECT-DATA-SECTION-RELOCATABLE (PE/COFF arm, c148 — the PE analog of the ELF c142 + Mach-O c147 `.o` data sections): a relocatable .obj DOES carry data — a global lands in `.rdata`/`.data`/`.bss` with a section-relative IMAGE_SYMBOL (SectionNumber = the section's 1-based ordinal, Value = the item's SECTION-RELATIVE offset — the COFF convention, unlike Mach-O's flat-address n_value) the FINAL linker binds. Same format-blind `AssembledModule.dataItems` producer path as ELF/Mach-O. D-LK-RELRO-CONST-DATA-RELOCATABLE (PE arm): a CONST global carrying LOAD-TIME relocations (a const function-pointer table / `int *const p = &x;` — sqlite's VFS method tables + `aSyscall[]`) lands in `relro` = a SECOND `.rdata`-named section (see the relro row) and the writer emits its OWN IMAGE_RELOCATION table (IMAGE_REL_AMD64_ADDR64, addend IN the 8-byte slot bytes — COFF's in-place-addend convention; IMAGE_RELOCATION has no addend column); a reloc-bearing MUTABLE pointer global lands in `data`. TLS (`tdata`/`tbss`) stays UNDECLARED — the linker's acceptsDataSection gate rejects it loud (the .obj walker emits no `.tls`/IMAGE_TLS_DIRECTORY64 machinery; that is the PE EXEC arm, D-CSUBSET-THREAD-LOCAL C3).

pe.$comment: IMAGE_FILE_HEADER identity. machine = IMAGE_FILE_MACHINE_AMD64 (0x8664). characteristics = 0 — relocatable .obj carries no file-level flags (link.exe sets image-level flags when producing the .exe/.dll).

sections.$comment: Executable code. PE Characteristics = IMAGE_SCN_CNT_CODE (0x20) | IMAGE_SCN_ALIGN_16BYTES (0x500000) | IMAGE_SCN_MEM_EXECUTE (0x20000000) | IMAGE_SCN_MEM_READ (0x40000000) = 0x60500020. PE's `type` field is repurposed to carry Characteristics (which encodes alignment via IMAGE_SCN_ALIGN_*BYTES bits); `flags` is unused; `addrAlign` MUST be 0 for PE rows (validate-rejected — PE encodes alignment in Characteristics, not the substrate's `addrAlign` field).
sections.name: .text

sections.$comment: D-LK-OBJECT-DATA-SECTION-RELOCATABLE (PE arm, c148): read-only initialized data (string literals, const globals WITHOUT relocations) — exactly where cl.exe places it in a .obj. Characteristics (`type`) = IMAGE_SCN_CNT_INITIALIZED_DATA (0x40) | IMAGE_SCN_MEM_READ (0x40000000) = 0x40000040 = 1073741888 — DELIBERATELY WITHOUT IMAGE_SCN_ALIGN_*BYTES bits: the .obj walker ORs in the align class computed from the H1-raised layout alignment (max of every member item's alignment) at emit time, exactly the per-contribution align class cl.exe itself stamps (e.g. an 8-byte-aligned .rdata contribution carries 0x40400040). addrAlign MUST stay 0 (validate-rejected on PE rows — alignment lives in Characteristics, never the substrate field).
sections.name: .rdata

sections.$comment: D-LK-OBJECT-DATA-SECTION-RELOCATABLE (PE arm, c148): writable initialized data (mutable globals, `int counter = 7;`). Characteristics (`type`) = IMAGE_SCN_CNT_INITIALIZED_DATA (0x40) | IMAGE_SCN_MEM_READ (0x40000000) | IMAGE_SCN_MEM_WRITE (0x80000000) = 0xC0000040 = 3221225536 — no align bits (walker-computed; see the rodata row). A reloc-bearing MUTABLE pointer global also lands here and the walker emits its IMAGE_RELOCATION records against this section (VirtualAddress = the slot's section-relative offset).
sections.name: .data

sections.$comment: D-LK-OBJECT-DATA-SECTION-RELOCATABLE (PE arm, c148): zero-initialized data (tentative globals `int g;` — DSS commits tentatives to a real `.bss` definition, the gcc -fno-common shape, NOT the MSVC COMMON-symbol form). Characteristics (`type`) = IMAGE_SCN_CNT_UNINITIALIZED_DATA (0x80) | IMAGE_SCN_MEM_READ (0x40000000) | IMAGE_SCN_MEM_WRITE (0x80000000) = 0xC0000080 = 3221225600 — no align bits (walker-computed). COFF .obj header convention (cl.exe-witnessed, dumpbin-confirmed): the bss span lives in SizeOfRawData with PointerToRawData = 0 and VirtualSize = 0 — the FILE stores no bytes; the final linker reserves SizeOfRawData zero-fill bytes.
sections.name: .bss

sections.$comment: D-LK-RELRO-CONST-DATA-RELOCATABLE (PE arm, c148): relocated-read-only const data — a CONST global carrying LOAD-TIME relocations (a const function-pointer table / `int *const p = &x;`). COFF has NO relro segment concept: MSVC places reloc-bearing const data in read-only `.rdata` and the LINKED image base-relocates it (the loader applies IMAGE_REL_BASED_DIR64 into the slot before the page is mapped read-only) — cl.exe-witnessed: `int (*const table[])(void)` lands in `.rdata` (0x40400040) with ADDR64 relocations. So this row is `.rdata`-CLASS under the SAME `.rdata` NAME but as its OWN row → the walker emits it as a SECOND `.rdata` section header, which COFF explicitly permits (link.exe merges same-name contributions into one image section). A distinct row (rather than folding into the rodata row) keeps the .o discipline the ELF `.data.rel.ro` / Mach-O `__DATA,__const` mirrors use: reloc-bearing rodata stays fail-loud while relro items get their own IMAGE_RELOCATION table. Characteristics (`type`) = 0x40000040 = 1073741888 — identical class to the rodata row, no align bits (walker-computed).
sections.name: .rdata

sections.$comment: D-LK-OBJECT-CARRIES-NO-SUMMARY-OR-MIR-SECTION. The per-module LINK-TIME-OPTIMIZATION SUMMARY. Characteristics = IMAGE_SCN_CNT_INITIALIZED_DATA (0x00000040) | IMAGE_SCN_MEM_DISCARDABLE (0x02000000) = 33554496. That pair is PE's spelling of non-ALLOC, and it is spelled as two facts rather than one: the section HAS file content, and the linker must DISCARD it rather than map it. IMAGE_SCN_MEM_READ is deliberately ABSENT -- a section with no memory-access characteristic is not placed in the image, which is what keeps a summary-carrying object linkable by link.exe/lld into a byte-identical program. ⚠ THE NAME IS SEVEN CHARACTERS ON PURPOSE: a COFF section header's Name field is EIGHT bytes, and a longer name has to be spilled into the string table as `/nnnn` -- a second encoding this writer does not need to reach for. PAIRED with the `.dssmir` row below; the SPLIT is the whole economy (see the summary/MIR note in section_kind.hpp).
sections.name: .dsssum

sections.$comment: D-LK-OBJECT-CARRIES-NO-SUMMARY-OR-MIR-SECTION. The module's serialized MIR body -- the LARGE half of the pair. Same Characteristics as the summary row above and for the same reasons; the two differ in PAYLOAD, never in wire treatment. Seven characters, for the same eight-byte Name field.
sections.name: .dssmir

relocations.$comment: 32-bit PC-relative (call / jmp rel32). IMAGE_REL_AMD64_REL32 = 4. `kind` = 1 matches x86_64.target.json's `rel32` row. link.exe handles the rel32 RIP-bias intrinsically (PE convention: the patch site holds whatever bytes the assembler wrote; the linker computes `target_va - (section_va + VA + 4)` and ADDS the stored value). The assembler writes 0x00000000 at the patch site — addend=0 is the PE convention for call/jmp rel32.
relocations.name: IMAGE_REL_AMD64_REL32

relocations.$comment: D-LK-PE-OBJ-ARM-CARRIES-NO-UNWIND-INFO: image-relative 32-bit (an RVA). IMAGE_REL_AMD64_ADDR32NB = 3; `kind` = 6 matches x86_64.target.json's `imagerel32` row, whose `imageRelative: true` is what tells the writer this row — and NOT the ADDR32 row directly above — carries a `RUNTIME_FUNCTION` field. This is the relocation the `.pdata` / `.xdata` emitter needs: three per RUNTIME_FUNCTION (BeginAddress and EndAddress against `.text`, UnwindInfoAddress against `.xdata`), plus one per UNWIND_INFO exception-handler field, with the addend stamped in the section bytes since COFF has no addend column. ⚠ ADDR32 IS NOT A SUBSTITUTE: it writes a full VA where the unwinder expects an offset from the image base.
relocations.name: IMAGE_REL_AMD64_ADDR32NB
